the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
job: a paid position of regular employment or a task to do
She found a part-time job at the local bakery.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
machines: devices with moving parts that perform tasks
Modern washing machines use far less water than older models.
keep: to continue having or doing something; to maintain
Please keep this document safe until the meeting next week.
failing: Despite failing twice, she kept trying until she passed.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
take: to get hold of, remove, or carry something
Please take a seat while you wait for the doctor.
computers: electronic devices that process data and perform tasks
The school gave every student access to computers in the library.
took: past tense of take; obtained, seized, or required something
Computers took the jobs we thought were hardest, and left the ones a child can do.
jobs: paid positions of employment or tasks
New factories created thousands of jobs in the region.
we: used to refer to the speaker and one or more other people
We forget most of what we just learned within a day.
thought: past tense of think; formed an opinion or belief in the mind
Computers took the jobs we thought were hardest, and left the ones a child can do.
were: past tense of 'be', used for plural or 'you'
The missing words had to be invented, and many were.
hardest: Learning to listen was the hardest part of the course for him.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
left: remaining after others have gone or been used
Only a few seats were left by the time we arrived.
ones: particular items or people already mentioned or understood
The smaller phones sell better than the larger ones this year.
child: a young human being below the age of full physical development
Every child in the class received a new set of books.
can: used to express ability or possibility
Anyone with an internet connection can join the online course.
do: to perform an action, or an auxiliary verb used in questions and negatives
What do you usually do on weekends?
fifty: The stadium can hold up to fifty thousand people.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
ago: back in the past; before the present time
They moved to this city nearly ten years ago.
people: human beings in general, considered as a group of individuals
Many people prefer walking to work during the warm summer months.
asked: put a question to someone or requested something
He asked the librarian where he could find books on astronomy.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
would: used to express a hypothetical or past future action
Fifty years ago, people asked which jobs machines would take first.
first: coming before all others in order or time
She was the first person to arrive at the meeting.
answers: responses given to questions or problems
The teacher collected the answers and began grading them that evening.
seemed: gave the impression of being something
The plan seemed reasonable until the costs were calculated.
obvious: easy to see or understand; clear
It was obvious from her face that something was wrong.
anything: If you need anything during the trip, just call me.
requiring: Tasks requiring careful judgement were left to senior staff.
hard: difficult; not easy, or solid to the touch
It was hard to concentrate with all that noise outside.
thinking: the activity of using the mind to consider or reason
Careful thinking helped her avoid a costly mistake.
go: to move or travel from one place to another
We should go before the traffic gets worse.
early: before the usual or expected time
She always arrives early for important meetings.
only: and no one or nothing more besides; just
Only a handful of tickets remained by the time we arrived.
hands: the parts of the body at the ends of the arms
Wash your hands before you start cooking.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality
It can be difficult to stay calm during an emergency.
safe: free from danger or risk of harm
The children were kept safe during the storm.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
long: having a great length or duration
It was a long journey across three different countries.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
both: the two of something, referring to two things together
Both students finished the exam well before the time limit.
guesses: estimates or opinions formed without certain knowledge
Their guesses about the final score were wildly different.
turned: past tense of turn; changed direction or became something different
Both guesses turned out to be backwards.
out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
backwards: in the direction of the back; in reverse
He accidentally stepped backwards and knocked over the vase.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
now: at the present time; at this moment
Now is a good time to start saving for retirement.
better: of higher quality or more suitable than something else
The second recipe turned out much better than the first attempt.
than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
person: a human being regarded as an individual
Every person in the room agreed that the plan needed changes.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
chess: a board game for two players using pieces of different powers
He learned to play chess from his grandfather as a child.
reading: the act of looking at and understanding written words
Reading before bed has become part of her nightly routine.
column: a vertical line of numbers, text, or figures in a table
He scanned the last column of the spreadsheet for errors.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
numbers: figures used to count or measure amounts; plural of number
The report is full of numbers that few people bother to check.
spotting: noticing or detecting something, often something unusual
Spotting the error early saved the company a lot of money.
pattern: a regular, repeated way in which something happens or is arranged
Analysts noticed a clear pattern in the company's sales figures.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
million: The charity raised over a million dollars for disaster relief.
records: written or stored accounts of facts or events
hồ sơ, dữ liệu ghi chép
The library keeps records of every book ever borrowed.
these: used to refer to people or things nearby or just mentioned
These shoes are far more comfortable than my old ones.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
treated: past tense of treat; dealt with or given medical care
These were once treated as the highest kinds of intelligence.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
highest: greatest in height or degree; superlative of high
This peak is the highest point in the entire range.
kinds: The market sells many kinds of fruit imported from other countries.
intelligence: the ability to learn, understand, and reason well
Artificial intelligence is changing the way many industries operate.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
turns: present tense of turn, used with he/she/it; changes direction
When the frame begins to lean to the left, the front wheel turns slightly to the left as well.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
written: expressed in the form of text rather than speech
được viết, ở dạng chữ viết
For centuries, Hebrew was written and read but rarely spoken at home.
down: toward a lower position or level
Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.
rules: official instructions stating what may or may not be done
New traffic rules were introduced to reduce accidents.
consider: think carefully about something before making a decision
Please consider all the options before signing the contract.
folding: the act of bending something over on itself
Folding the laundry neatly takes more patience than washing it.
towel: a piece of absorbent cloth used for drying
manages: succeeds in doing something, or controls it
Somehow she always manages to arrive exactly on time.
seconds: units of time, sixty of which make a minute
The whole process took only a few seconds to complete.
robot: a machine capable of carrying out tasks automatically
The factory installed a robot to handle heavy lifting.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
where: It changes where the effort goes, away from the comfortable hours of reading.
cloth: woven or felted fabric made from fibres
She wiped the table with a damp cloth.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
fold: a line or crease made by bending something over on itself
She pressed a sharp fold into the paper before cutting it.
looking: He spent the afternoon looking for his missing keys.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
shape: the outward form or outline of something
The cookie cutter gave the biscuits a star shape.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
lifted: raised something to a higher position
The crane lifted the heavy container onto the ship.
changes: plural of change; alterations or differences from before
The new law brought major changes to how taxes are collected.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
decides: makes a choice or judgment after considering options
The referee ultimately decides whether the goal counts.
holds: remains true or applicable; third person singular of hold
The same rule holds for every branch of the company.
across: from one side of something to the other
A narrow bridge stretches across the river near the old mill.
many: Many residents still remember the flood of that year.
trades: plural of trade; skilled jobs, or acts of buying and selling
The pattern holds across many trades.
sorting: the act of arranging things into groups or a particular order
Sorting the recycling takes about ten minutes every week.
parcels: packages wrapped for sending, especially by post
The courier delivered several parcels to our office this morning.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
address: the details of where a person lives or a place is located
She wrote her new address on the back of the envelope.
easy: The test was easy enough that most students finished early.
automate: to make a process work by machine instead of people
The factory plans to automate its packaging line next year.
picking: the act of choosing or gathering something
He spent the afternoon picking apples with his grandchildren.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
unfamiliar: Sorting parcels by address is easy to automate; picking an unfamiliar object out of a box is not.
object: a physical thing that can be seen or touched
A strange object was found lying on the beach this morning.
crowded: full of people; having little empty space
The train was so crowded that several passengers had to stand.
box: a container with straight sides, usually square or rectangular
He packed his old books into a cardboard box.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
scan: an image produced by examining something with a detecting device
The doctor studied the scan carefully before making a diagnosis.
increasingly: more and more as time goes on
Remote work has become increasingly common since the pandemic.
done: Have you done your homework for tomorrow yet?
software: the programs and instructions used to operate computers
The company develops software for managing hospital records.
persuading: convincing someone to do or believe something
Persuading the committee took several meetings and a great deal of patience.
frightened: The frightened child hid behind her mother during the storm.
patient: a person who is receiving medical treatment
The nurse checked the patient's temperature every hour.
sit: to rest with the body supported on the buttocks
Please sit down and make yourself comfortable while you wait.
still: continuing to be the case; even more so
Despite the rain, the match still went ahead as planned.
reason: a cause or explanation for something
Nobody knew the real reason for his sudden resignation.
learned: gained knowledge or skill through study or experience
She learned to cook traditional dishes from her grandmother.
difficult: not easy to do or understand
Learning a new language can be difficult at first.
things: plural of thing; objects, ideas, or matters
She packed her things and left the apartment quietly.
recently: He recently moved to a new apartment closer to his office.
over: during the whole of a period of time; more than
Prices have risen steadily over the past five years.
millions: very large numbers, several times a million
Millions of people watched the event live online.
walking: the act of travelling on foot
Walking, gripping and reading a face were solved long before anyone could explain how.
gripping: holding something tightly with the hand
Gripping the rope tightly, she climbed slowly up the cliff.
face: to be forced to deal with a difficult situation
Small businesses face rising costs again this year.
solved: found an answer to a problem or difficulty
The mystery was finally solved after years of investigation.
before: earlier than a particular time or event
Please arrive at the airport before your flight is due to leave.
anyone: Anyone interested in the workshop should sign up before Friday.
could: past tense of can, used to express ability or possibility
She could speak three languages fluently by the age of ten.
explain: to make something clear by describing it in detail
Walking and reading a face were solved long before anyone could explain how.
how: She explained how the machine works in simple terms.
nobody: not a single person; no one
Nobody expected the small team to win the championship.
write: to produce text using a pen, keyboard or similar tool
Trying to write the same content from memory feels far worse than rereading it.
because: They cancelled the picnic because it started to rain.
ever: Nobody can write down rules that nobody ever actually knew.
knew: had knowledge or awareness of something (past of know)
Nobody knew the full story until the report was published.
them: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the object
I called them yesterday but nobody answered the phone.
repeats: happens again in the same way
The chorus repeats three times before the song ends.
look: to direct one's eyes in order to see
Look both ways carefully before crossing the busy street.
nothing: There was nothing left in the fridge by Friday evening.
alike: The two houses look almost alike from the outside.
predictions: statements about what will happen in the future
The company's predictions about future sales were far too optimistic.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
tend: to be likely to do or be something, usually
Older houses in this area tend to have thicker walls.
made: The table was made entirely from reclaimed wood.
who: used to ask about or refer to a person
The extra heat is dangerous for anyone who cannot afford to cool their home.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
watched: looked at something for a period of time
Predictions are made by people who have only watched the work from outside.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
outside: not inside; in or to a place beyond the boundary of something
The children played outside until it grew dark.
almost: very nearly but not completely or entirely
She almost missed the last train home after the concert ended.
looks: appears to be, has a certain appearance
The sky looks heavy with rain this afternoon.
like: similar to, or in the same way as
Her handwriting looks a lot like her mother's.
list: a set of items written one after another
She made a list of groceries before going to the market.
steps: a series of actions taken to achieve something
Follow these simple steps to reset your password.
spend: to use time or money on something
They spend every summer visiting their grandparents in the countryside.
week: The loss is fastest at the start, then slows over the following week.
beside: next to or at the side of something
She sat beside her grandmother during the long train journey home.
doing: What are you doing this weekend?
small: not large in size, amount, or degree
They live in a small apartment near the city center.
part: a piece or portion of a whole
Only a small part of the report dealt with financial risks.
wrapped: The list turns out to be the small part, wrapped in judgement nobody wrote down.
judgement: an opinion or decision formed after careful thought
Her judgement about the risk turned out to be correct.
wrote: The list turns out to be the part nobody ever wrote down.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
mean: A red light at a crossing means drivers must stop.
such: of the type already mentioned or described
Such behaviour will not be tolerated in the workplace.
forever: for all future time; without ever ending
She promised to remember that summer forever.
based: having something as a foundation or starting point
The film is based on a true story from the 1980s.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
feels: The fabric feels soft and warm against the skin.
human: relating to or characteristic of people
con người, thuộc về con người
The robot cannot yet match human judgment in complex situations.
being: existing, or the fact of existing in a particular state
Being tired all week, she decided to cancel her weekend plans.
poor: not good in quality, ability, or amount; weak
The bridge was closed after inspectors found its poor condition dangerous.
record: a written or stored account of facts or events
The hospital keeps a detailed record of every patient's treatment.
useful: able to be used effectively for a purpose; helpful
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but whether anyone can say how it is done.
question: /ˈkwestʃən/
n
a sentence asked to get information or express doubt
câu hỏi, vấn đề
Nobody could answer the teacher's difficult question about gravity.
query
inquiry
issue
whether: used to express doubt or choice between alternatives
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but how it is done.
task: a piece of work that must be done
Sorting the mail was the first task of her morning shift.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
say: It is hard to say exactly when the tradition began.
exactly: in a way that is precise or correct in every detail
A fact heard once looks exactly like one that will never be needed.
